settings.heading: The Out-the-Door Gloves
settings.body:
There is a particular hour — before eight, the coat already on, the keys somewhere — when nobody wants to be making decisions. These are for that hour.

They are the plainest possible answer to it. Chocolate lambskin, cut close to the hand, three fine lines of stitching down the back and a plain edge just past the wrist. Nothing to fasten. Nothing to think about.

You put them on at the door, and take them off when you arrive. Then they wait in the purse for the walk home.
settings.pull_quote: A little preparedness. Very good taste.

settings.heading: Chosen, Not Made
settings.note:
The house did not make these. It went looking, and stopped at Glove Story, in France, who have been making gloves properly for a long time and did not need our help.

That is the other half of the work. Some things we make — the perfume is blended here, by hand, in small batches. Some things we find. Both take the same eye, and we would rather tell you which is which.

settings.label: The colourway
settings.text: Chocolate — a deep, even brown that sits beside the Café Noir of The Brownstone Tote without trying to match it.

settings.label: Choosing yours
settings.text: Skip the tape measure. Medium is the standard hand; Small is cut for a narrower one. If you land between two sizes, take the smaller.
